first.rationale:
Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are funnel-health problems, not price problems, and the inherited record supports onboarding work from two partially independent angles (memory_31 on signup field reduction lifting SMB activation, memory_86 on shortened onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value). A single onboarding experiment plausibly moves both declining metrics, and its gains are margin-neutral, which matters given the stated objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue rather than raw acquisition.

I am spending verification on memory_73 first because it is the memory most likely to capture the slot and the one whose phrasing shows the strongest signs of consolidation drift: it stacks four distinct claims (acquisition lift, revenue lift, reduced time-to-first-value, generalization across both billing plans) into one summary, and breadth claims like 'held across both billing plans' are exactly the kind of detail that gets added during summarization rather than measured. If the archived record turns out to be a narrow single-segment test, then the obvious competitor-response move is far weaker than the memory implies. Second verification goes to memory_86, since it is the load-bearing support for my intended action and I would rather discover its weakness before committing than after; memory_31 covers adjacent ground, so if memory_86 thins out I still have partial support.

Downstream value risk is flagged for two reasons. Discount-led responses to a competitor's entry pricing tend to buy price-sensitive, low-retention accounts and reset price expectations, which can raise short-term revenue while degrading the qualified-revenue objective. Separately, every memory here is a consolidated summary with the source archived; acting on them at scale silently promotes unverified summaries into fresh evidence, compounding any drift already present. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is set aside because it does not address the SMB-side declines driving this quarter.

I am treating this as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout: the supporting memories are consistent but unverified until the archive returns, and the declines could stem from a product or cohort change that no prior experiment covers. If verification shows memory_86 was narrow, I would drop to a small guarded test rather than change direction.
